messages:
Maria: Quick sync — UX question: when we auto-fallback into a 'degrade' model variant, should the Console show an explicit 'Degraded' toggle (on/off) per-route or just an immutable banner with a link to the audit?
Kai: My vote: immutable banner + link. Operators shouldn't casually flip fallback behavior. We need an approval flow for overrides. :no_entry:
Jonah: Agreed on approval. Also, how do we present WHY it fell back? Error triggers are noisy (timeouts, 5xx, kv cache miss). We should show the top 3 signals and a confidence score.
Taylor: Confidence score is good but we need to avoid leaking PII in traces. For some customers we might have to redact examples and sampling. Maybe the toggle controls sampling detail level: off / summary / full (requires audit role).
Ellen: UX note — 'toggle' implies an immediate state change. If it's an operator-only override it should be labeled 'Temporary override (requires approval)' and include TTL. Otherwise folks will flip it during incidents and mask root cause.
Maria: Good point. TTL + who/why metadata. Also product asked for a one-click 'replay' button to reproduce the fallback locally (shadow run). That needs the exact request + model version + routing policy snapshot. Can we store that in the audit?
Kai: We can store a compact snapshot. Storage size is the issue. Proposal: store 1) trigger event id, 2) routing policy hash, 3) minimal request fingerprint + link to full payload in object store (if customer allows).
Jonah: From infra: we must avoid storing raw prompts by default. Use a pointer pattern: audit contains a link to encrypted payload with ACL. Console shows a redacted preview and a 'request for full payload' button (audited).
Taylor: For the UI, show chronology: fallback triggered -> attempted fallback -> resolution. Each step has small icons (⚠️, ↩️, ✅) and a hover tooltip with the signal names.
Maria: Edgecase: what about oscillation? If the policy flips back/forth we should surface an 'oscillation detected' badge and auto-throttle overrides.
Kai: Add hysteresis controls in policy editor: min duration in fallback, cool-down window, and max override frequency. Those should be in the rollout policy, not the Console toggle.
Ellen: Related: telemetry sampling. Ops want high fidelity during incidents, but billing teams worry about cost. Maybe a per-customer sampling multiplier that can be bumped temporarily via the override flow (with billing approval flag).
Jonah: Implementation sketch:
```
fallback_event: {
  id: "evt_123",
  reason: "model_timeout",
  signals: ["latency: p95>1s", "error_rate: 5xx>3%"],
  routing_policy_hash: "abc123",
  snapshot_pointer: "s3://redwood-audit/evt_123.enc",
  override: { user: "Ellen", expires_at: "2026-06-01T15:00:00Z" }
}
```
Maria: Perfect. For the Console copy, avoid heavy jargon. Example: 'Traffic automatically routed to a lower-latency variant to preserve availability. Learn more.' Link goes to audit view.
Taylor: Accessibility + mobile: make sure the banner isn't full-screen and that the audit page is searchable by event id and route.
Kai: One more policy question: should we allow partial fallbacks (sample X% traffic) via the UI? Operators want quick 'ramp to fallback' controls.
Ellen: Yeah, show a small slider (0–100%) with a confirm modal explaining risk and showing estimated cost change. Track that in audit too.
Maria: OK action items: Kai — design approval flow + hystereses in policy editor. Jonah — redact-by-default audit pointer impl and ACL spec. Taylor — UI mocks for banner, override modal, and replay button. Ellen — copy + compliance notes. I'll schedule a 30m sync after mocks.
deploy-bot: Note: canary 0.12.3 deployed to staging with fallback-audit endpoints; tests passed. :white_check_mark:
